answer: Scheduled Inlet Beacon Windows. Each identity may submit work only through a rotating inlet opened by a shared beacon pulse; the window is narrow and its phase is unpredictable. Traffic shape is enforced: submissions arriving outside the tide of scheduled pulses are dropped, and consistent off-phase activity flags the identity. An attacker must maintain each clone through many idle cycles to learn phase, paying sustained compute and latency per identity rather than a one-time fee.
